... might as well post a few more pics 8 months later :)

Customer came in with this little engine block that was hurting a bit, a piston rod broke and saw the light for the first time since its defective manufacturing days.

First I clean up the edges and sprayed penetrating dye on it, then I sprayed the developer on and it exposed the cracks. I did this inside and outside so I wouldn't miss anything.

After that I got my favorite die grinder and went to town on those cracks. I also broke off a little chunk that was barely holding on and made a patch out of plain 1/4" steel.

Now it was time to start welding, the first step was to wrap it in blankets, plug the holes with bolts to avoid spatter getting in the threads and preheat it. The patch I tacked in place before hand.

The procedure is to make short welds (max 1") and then peen them which means banging the shit out of them with a chipping hammer to prevent surface cracking. I did a layer on the outside first, grinded down a bit around the patch and filled the chamfers up. Then I did the same on the inside.

Once the hot work was done I started filling it with vermiculite (I'm sure the customer enjoyed cleaning out the dust) and then I wrapped it in blankets for 24hrs so it would cool down slowly.

The next day it was ready for pick up..

I never heard back from the customer so I'm safely assuming that no news is good news and the repair's holding well. Total cost to him was roughly 1000$.
